Week-1 planned running minutes (walks excluded; walk/jog counts its jogging minutes) <= current reported or wearable-conservative weekly running minutes; when current exposure is zero or unknown, or the athlete is a novice, only the listed establishment entries (walk/jog ladder step 0, the 15-20 minute easy entry) are used.
Week-1 long run <= the longest current run reported; rounding may not exceed it.
No quality, strides or race-effort work in week 1 except a current familiar quality task that fits inside the week-1 running ceiling.
Unknowns are emitted with one of the four categories; ASK only for facts that change the first program (eligibility, goal, chosen days and session time, event date); clinical flags route to a human.

An intake pause needs a structured nonclinical reason category; free text alone is ASK and can only add CLINICAL or ASK outcomes.

A non-novice whose longest current run or weekly running is below run.minimumSessionMinutes starts on the walk/jog ladder at the highest step whose jogging per session is <= the longest current run and <= current weekly running divided by the walk/jog exposures of the week; no week-1 session holds more running than the longest current run (D42).

Intake loads: a pound value converts to kilograms at the nearest 0.5 kg and keeps the reported value; any other or missing unit leaves the load unknown and asked; a reported known dose above six sets starts at six.

An eligibility flag that means yes in any form (true, 1, yes, y, sim, si or sí, trimmed, in any letter case and with or without accents) routes CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED; any other non-boolean flag leaves eligibility unassessed (ASK), never clearance and never assumed illness.
limitations: Onboarding facts are self-report; wearable history may be partial.
No evidence validates the exact starter doses or establishment length.

The interruption-reason text screen is a lexicon heuristic; any further lexical residual is an owned open gap, and the structured category plus current eligibility (dated after the break, every clinical flag false) remain the primary defence.
The familiar start rests on self-reported longest and weekly running; equivalence of intermittent and continuous jogging is unstudied.

Athletes with strength class NONE complete unloaded or light-implement practice before any effort-guided loaded set; the first loaded exposure is at most 2 sets at RIR >= 3.

The establishment instruction describes an ascending ramp: start with the lightest available load and add the smallest increment between preparatory sets while at least the target reserve remains with stable technique; the working load is the heaviest such load; load and convention are recorded.
No kilogram is derived from sex, body mass, another exercise or implement; a stale or differently configured known load is only a hint or ceiling.

After establishment, a load or repetition step requires a logged set record meeting target repetitions with reserve >= prescribed RIR - 1; otherwise the dose holds. A logged load above the planned load is adopted only when that exposure meets this criterion and only up to one smallest increment above the plan, never above a re-establishment ceiling; otherwise the planned load stays the reference and the logged load is asked about. A logged load at or below the plan is executed evidence; a changed known load is a modification (D44).
RIR is treated as approximate (about one repetition of error); technique and comfort govern continuation and stopping.
Fail-closed: no ESTABLISH rows are emitted when this boundary is not enabled.

A load logged on an establishment row becomes a prescribed numeric (KNOWN) load only after the athlete confirms it (in kilograms or pounds, in the planned convention), after a second logged exposure of the exercise in a separate session (later, or earlier in the same week) within establishmentAgreementIncrements smallest increment of it, or when it lies within one smallest increment of the athlete's own load hint in the same convention. Until then the next exposure is FROM_LOG with no number, its instructions describe effort-guided selection only and never point to the logged value (D48), and the logged value is asked about. Numeric plausibility of a confirmed or repeated value is Data-owned (D45).

Loads are kilograms in the engine: a pound value (intake or log) converts at the nearest 0.5 kg and keeps the reported value; another or missing unit, or a logged convention different from the planned one, is never adopted and is asked about; no prescription carries pounds or a known load above 500 kg.

An above-plan logged load is adopted only when that exercise's gate for the week is ADVANCE or EARNED; a missing reps-in-reserve log, an adverse response or a converging-fatigue hold keeps the planned load and the load is asked about (D44).
limitations: Evidence for RIR accuracy in never-trained adults is thin.
Self-selected loads by novices tend to be conservative; early weeks may under-dose.
Self-selected load evidence is abstract-level; plausibility rules for logged values are Data-owned.
The agreement tolerance is a data-consistency rule; plausibility of repeated or confirmed values is Data-owned and not yet defined.

Operational values are reversible coaching choices inside the envelope, never physiological thresholds, injury-prevention rules, readiness scores, finish-time promises or individual-response predictions.
Steps advance only on executed comparable work without an adverse signal; nothing progresses from elapsed calendar time alone; completed history and official plan state stay immutable.

One progression dimension per session type per week; EARNED may release a step the cadence would otherwise hold or skip a consolidation hold, but never adds more than one step on any dimension in a week, and is unavailable in WALK_JOG, RESTART and RETURN modes.

Every step requires executed comparable sessions without an adverse signal in the gating week; quality/strides activation, block-boundary set increases and ladder steps count executed weeks, never calendar weeks.

Single-run ceiling (operational.run.singleRunCeiling): no planned run other than the race exceeds the longest completed run of the preceding 30 days (completed-work ledger, the intake-reported longest current run while within 30 days of intake, a valid return demonstration) by more than one stepMinutes; walk/jog ladder sessions and walks follow the ladder, whose start never holds more jogging per session than the longest current run (D42); with nothing completed in the window the reviewed entry (return.entryRunMinutes) is the ceiling in every week, not only the first.

When the 30-day reference run is under 50 minutes, the 5-minute step exceeds 10% of it; the step stays response-gated, is disclosed, and is never combined with another single-session increase in the same week.

Strength ADVANCE requires logged target repetitions and minimum logged RIR >= prescribed RIR - 1; EARNED requires minimum logged RIR >= prescribed RIR + 2 on two comparable exposures outside consolidation; a known-load or bodyweight repetition or load step requires a logged set for that exercise in the gating week; missing logs or unknown logged RIR hold the dose without regression; a logged load above the plan never becomes the reference unless that exposure met the ADVANCE criterion (D44).

longRunShareOfWeeklyMinutesMax limits long-run growth in weeks with at least three running sessions; the cap holds the long run and never shortens it below the typical easy run or the last build week's long run; consolidation, taper and return reductions are separate rules.
Transition magnitudes (restart step and switch point, walk/jog exit dose, consolidation reduction, post-event redevelopment) are declared in the policy, not hard-coded.
Repeated adverse responses (two comparable within 14 days at the current dose after any regression) regress one step; a single adverse response holds.

A run dimension or exercise with no executed session in the reviewed week holds: it never counts as an executed week, never advances a walk/jog step, never unlocks quality or strides and never converts a walk. In a conditional projection a week with no planned session of a dimension likewise never counts as executed for it (D46).
After an exercise is re-established by effort, its earlier set count returns at most one set per executed week.

Return-entry and return-step exposures never count toward a block-boundary set increase; after the return steps the set count comes back at most one set per executed week to the last executed pre-break set count (D49, shared with R6-NONCLINICAL-RETURN).
limitations: Step sizes, cadence and consolidation are operational, not evidence-derived optima.
Single-session injury association is observational and distance-based.
Strength progression evidence is from trained lifters over 8 weeks.
requiredRuntimeChanges: D49 (R6-NONCLINICAL-RETURN, shared with R6-PLANNED-PROGRESSION) r6-program.mjs advanceStrength (block-boundary credit, blocksDone) and strengthDose (return step 2 and the first weeks after the return), and policy operational.return: after a moderate or long nonclinical interruption the strength return is one set at RIR >= 4, then the base set count minus one at RIR 3, then the normal dose. Two things break the declared ceiling and the one-set-per-executed-week rule. (1) A return-entry or return-step exposure in the last week of a development block (often a consolidation week) is credited as a completed block, so the first post-return week adds a block-boundary set. (2) Step 2 is computed from the base set count, not from the dose prescribed before the break. In probe section U, 7 of 17 return timelines (moderate and long) jump from 2 to 4 back-squat sets in one week and/or exceed the sets prescribed in the last week before the break; for example s1-d35 goes 3 sets before the break, then 1, 2 and 4, and s5-d14 goes 4, then 1, 2 and 4. Exercises first set up in the return-entry week (the author-found change) follow the same path. This contradicts R6-NONCLINICAL-RETURN conditions 7 and 11 (at most moderateStepsToPrior steps to the prior executed dose; historical maxima are ceilings) and R6-PLANNED-PROGRESSION conditions 5 and 13 (block-boundary set increases count executed development weeks; after re-establishment by effort the earlier set count returns at most one set per executed week). The defect predates R6-POLICY-4 (the FREEZE-1 source has the same credit and step-2 formula); I did not detect it in rounds 1 to 7. Required: (a) return-entry and return-step exposures never count toward a block-boundary set increase; (b) after the return steps the set count returns to the last executed pre-break set count at most one set per executed week, consolidation and taper reductions applying on top, and goes above it only through a block completed with non-return executed exposures; (c) declare this in operational.return, together with the load cap as the runtime applies it (during the return steps the cap is the current return reference: the adopted entry load, otherwise the load before the break); (d) add the probe-U timelines s1-d35, s3-d21 and s5-d14 as regression tests.

Steps advance only on executed comparable work without an adverse signal; nothing progresses from elapsed calendar time alone; completed history and official plan state stay immutable.

Supported events are 10K and half-marathon only; one taper week plus the race week, progressive: taper-week easy runs within taperWeekRunVolumeRange and the long run within taperWeekLongRunRange of the executed peak; taper quality total work minutes within taperQualityWorkRange; race-week easy runs within raceWeekRunVolumeRange; the policy states these are per-session fractions.

Frequency is maintained; intensity is maintained only through work already executed in build/specific weeks; a race-effort touch at the policy dose >= raceWeekTouchMinDaysBeforeRace days before the race requires R6-RUN-QUALITY and an executed comparable quality session; shakeout strides require executed strides; otherwise easy.

Strength stays at a reduced dose: taper sets about taperStrengthSetFraction of the preceding dose at RIR >= 3; race week one session of raceWeekStrengthSets at RIR >= raceWeekStrengthMinimumRir no later than raceWeekStrengthMinDaysBeforeRace days before the race; no new exercise, load increase or rotation.

Post-event: no running before postEventFirstRunMinDaysAfterRace days; runs optional and easy within postEventEasyMinutes; one light strength session; redevelopment (NEXT_BLOCK) requires an eligibility and function assessment dated after the race; redevelopment fractions are declared in the policy.
The legacy path uses the athlete's event kind and only policy-declared fractions.
No finish-time, readiness or peak-performance claim.

Event proximity counts days to the race (raceWindowDays 6; 7 taper days per taper week before the window): race-window sessions have no long run and no quality, an optional shakeout the day before, at most one race-effort touch on the run day closest to the race that is >= raceWeekTouchMinDaysBeforeRace days out, and short easy runs; taper-day sessions take taper doses whichever calendar week they fall in; post-race sessions follow the post-event rules by days since the race; a race date marked unavailable is asked about.
In WALK_JOG or RESTART mode, taper-day, race-window and post-event run sessions are reductions or holds of the achieved session of that mode, never a continuous run the mode has not reached (D43a).

Race day is a completion prescription at conversational effort with walk breaks (jog bouts no longer than achieved), without strides and without an instruction to press, when the race-week mode is WALK_JOG, RESTART or RETURN, when the athlete was in WALK_JOG or RESTART mode in any week of the program before the race (D47), or for a half marathon whose achieved long run is below raceDayCompletion.halfMarathonAchievedLongRunBelowMinutes; race-day warm-up strides and shakeout strides for any athlete only after executed strides (D43b-c, R9).

Whenever race day is a completion, the event negotiation states the longest continuous run the plan reaches by race week (never 0 when runs were reached) and offers keep-with-walk-breaks or a later or shorter event; it may stay non-blocking for the preparatory weeks (D43d, D47).
In taper weeks and at the start of the next block the long run is never shorter than that week's easy run (R10).
Walk/jog and restart steps do not advance on taper, race-window or post-event days; the next block resumes the walk/jog ladder one step back.
limitations: Taper evidence is from trained athletes; recreational evidence observational.
Combined run+strength taper evidence is indirect.
Post-event recovery evidence is from a simulated half-marathon.
The 6-day race window and the 7-day taper-day split are operational; completion with walk breaks is supported only indirectly (run/walk trial in marathoners, abstract only).
Which rebuilt long run, if any, should exempt a walk/jog- or restart-class athlete from the completion default is not established; no exemption applies until one is declared and reviewed.

dossierAnswers.question: Q1 (D44): is "the exercise's gate this week is ADVANCE or EARNED" the right reading of the ADVANCE criterion, with a converging-fatigue HOLD also blocking above-plan adoption?
dossierAnswers.answer: Yes. The weekly exercise gate is ADVANCE exactly when target repetitions were met with minimum logged RIR at or above the prescription minus one and no adverse response, so ADVANCE or EARNED is the criterion I required. The gate is the first non-ADVANCE result across the week's exposures, which is conservative when an exercise appears twice. A missing RIR log holds, which is consistent with "missing effort is unknown". A converging-fatigue hold is an adverse signal, so blocking adoption there is consistent with "no adverse response". Probe M confirms every path. D44 is resolved.

dossierAnswers.question: Q2 (D45): one increment as the agreement tolerance; two agreeing logs in one week; two consistent but implausible logs adopted
dossierAnswers.answer: (a) Yes: one smallest increment is at or above the session-to-session variability of effort-selected loads for most loads (R6-S42, abstract), and it is the resolution of the equipment, so it is a sound consistency tolerance. (b) Yes, provided the two logs come from separate sessions, which the runtime ensures: a recording check gains as much from a second session in the same week as from one in a later week. (c) Accepted inside D45: my condition was that a single unconfirmed log never becomes a number, not that any number is plausible. Plausibility of repeated or athlete-confirmed values stays Data-owned and open. The mechanism is resolved; D48 (the pending row's first instruction) must still be fixed.

dossierAnswers.question: Q3 (return ceiling): during the return steps the cap is the current reference ("no increase yet")
dossierAnswers.answer: Confirmed. Before the entry load is adopted the cap is the load before the break; in return step 2 the runtime caps at the adopted entry load, so a heavier step-2 log is capped and asked about (probe O). That is stricter than the declared text ("above the load before the break") and matches the step-2 instruction "no increase yet". It is conservative for one week only, because normal progression resumes after the steps and strength is regained quickly after short breaks (R6-S43). Declare the rule as the runtime applies it, together with D49.

dossierAnswers.question: Q4 (author-found): the entry dose for every exposure of the entry week, and return step 2 for exercises first set up in it
dossierAnswers.answer: Confirmed for both. Every strength row of the return-entry week is one set at RIR >= 4, including later exposures of exercises first set up in that week, and those exercises continue to return step 2 (probe O). The week after step 2 is not acceptable yet, for those exercises and for known ones: return weeks earn a block-boundary set and step 2 is computed from the base set count, so in 7 of 17 return timelines the first post-return week jumps from 2 to 4 sets and/or exceeds the pre-break dose (D49, probe U). This predates R6-POLICY-4; I missed it in earlier rounds.

dossierAnswers.question: Q5 (R6): yes-meaning flags route CLINICAL; non-boolean no-meaning values stay ASK; a clinical status in any letter case routes CLINICAL
dossierAnswers.answer: Confirmed for all three. Probe Q: twelve yes-meaning forms route CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED in the intake and the review, and the legacy path does the same for generation and review. "false", "no", 0, "maybe", "yes.", null and 2 stay ASK (the legacy review returns HOLD). Keeping non-boolean no-meaning values as ASK is stricter than the interruption flag and correct for eligibility: an eligibility answer that is not a clean boolean has not been assessed, and unknown is neither clearance nor illness.

dossierAnswers.question: Q6 (R7): local negation makes a damage statement ASK; affirmed damage stays CLINICAL; a FAMILY note mentioning a baby is asked
dossierAnswers.answer: Accepted inside my owned gap. In probes J and R every locally negated damage statement in the three languages is ASK and none is NONCLINICAL; affirmed damage stays CLINICAL wherever else a negation sits, including "I don't think I broke my leg" and "Almost broke my ankle"; the round-7 residuals route CLINICAL or ASK; a baby mention in a FAMILY note costs one question. New residuals still screen NONCLINICAL with a nonclinical category: C-section, maternity leave, newborn, breastfeeding, miscarriage (in several languages), assault, minor procedures, stings, burns ("hand" is missing from the body-part list) and "nothing broken, just bruised". They are recorded as recommendation R11 and do not block, because the structured category and current eligibility remain the primary defence. Pregnancy and postpartum have a structured intake exclusion but no structured re-check at reviews and returns; that belongs in the structured intake design re-review required before any use beyond the offline reference.

dossierAnswers.question: Binding defects D42-D46 (round 7)
dossierAnswers.answer: D42 resolved (probe B: 0 of 128 raised starts above the longest current run; each start is the highest fitting step). D43 partly resolved: (a) mode-following event sessions, (c) strides only after executed strides and (e) declarations with tests are resolved; (b) and (d) narrowed the completion and negotiation trigger to the race-week mode, so athletes who leave the walk/jog ladder or a restart before a 10K race at race effort with no negotiation (D47). D44 resolved (probe M). D45 resolved in mechanism (probe N), with D48 left in the pending row's instructions. D46 resolved (probes L and P), with two conservative side effects recorded as R12 and R13.

dossierAnswers.answer: R6 adopted and accepted. R7 adopted and accepted inside the owned gap, with new residuals in R11. R9 adopted for the half marathon (achieved long run under 75 minutes); for walk/jog- or restart-built 10K racers it is now binding as D47; for EASY-class 10K racers with a short achieved long run it stays a recommendation. R10 adopted (probe A: 792 taper and next-block weeks, none with the long run shorter than the easy run). Author-found change: the entry week and step 2 are accepted; the following week is D49.
